text:
oliver: heads up — the new typescript SDK sample app failed in the edge smoke test after the release. stack trace is an import error in the Cloudflare worker runtime.

ci-bot: CI failure: publish-canary (edge-smoke) — exit code 1.

oliver: error from the runtime: `Uncaught TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier "../dist/index.cjs"` — it looks like the package published a .cjs entry in `main` but the edge runtime is trying to load ESM. sourcemaps also missing so stack traces are useless.

kevin: can you paste package.json from the published tarball?

oliver: sure — snippet from the tarball:
```json
{"name":"@redwood/inference-js","version":"0.13.4-canary","main":"dist/index.cjs","module":"dist/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","files":["dist"]}
```

maria: yep that's the problem. our publish job used rollup with `output.format = 'cjs'` for `main` but we left `module` pointing to the ESM build. edge sample tries to import the module path and ends up with dynamic import of a .cjs file which CF worker rejects. also no `engines` or `browser` field to hint bundlers.

sam: interesting — why are sourcemaps missing? I thought we had `sourcemap: true` in the rollup config.

kevin: the release script strips `*.map` from the tarball because the pipeline thought maps were sensitive. that filter used a glob that accidentally matched `dist/*.map` and `dist/*.d.ts.map` but our rollup emits `dist/index.mjs.map` and the strip step used wrong pattern — so maps were dropped.

hannah: can we add a quick guard in the release pipeline that validates the package after packing? e.g. check that `main` file exists and that `.map` files are present if `types` references them. this would have caught it.

oliver: agreed. for a hotfix i'm proposing: 1) republish a patch where `main` points to `dist/index.cjs` only for node targets and add `exports` map to make ESM import use `dist/index.mjs` explicitly; 2) restore sourcemaps and include `source` field; 3) add smoke test that runs a minimal ESM import in an edge runtime emulator.

kevin: also add a `postpack` test that unpacks the tarball and verifies `package.json` files exist with the referenced entries. i can add a lint rule for mismatched `main/module/exports`.

maria: small code suggestion for `package.json` export map: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
that lets node and bundlers pick the right file and prevents accidental dynamic import of CJS in ESM contexts.

sam: i'll open the canary revert + republish PR now. planning to also add the pipeline check Hannah suggested. @release-bot can we hold subsequent releases until the hotfix goes through?

release-bot: Release hold placed by sam — tag: canary-fix-180950. CI gates required: unit, canary-smoke, postpack-check.

oliver: thanks. after this we should update the sample app docs to explicitly show bundler-friendly imports (import from package root) and mention that Edge runtimes expect ESM entrypoints. small onboarding fix but will avoid confusion. :thumbsup:

hannah: +1. i'll add the test ticket to the release checklist and make a quick PR for the postpack validation.

kevin: leaving a note here: follow-up to add unit test for `types` presence and source map integrity. current bug caused a bad DX for customers importing from the pkg in edge environments.

oliver: filing the customer-facing postmortem draft now — will mention root cause: publish script glob and missing exports map.

ci-bot: reopened issue #4812 (sdk-publish-edge-entrypoint)

sam: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/274 — includes fixes and postpack test.

oliver: testing the canary locally in wrangler + node now. will update thread in 10m.

kevin: thanks everyone — clean and quick fix.
